draft.body_en:
Thanks Sam. Following up on the three schedules I sent on Friday:

1. The first failed collection was on Mon 12 Oct, a bank holiday. Should the retry have moved to Tue 13 Oct, or is it meant to wait for the next collection cycle?
2. Do the 214 accounts EE listed all share that same pattern, or are some failing for a different reason?
3. When the retry does run, could a customer be collected for both the missed and the current amount in one go?

EE are asking about point 3 for their customer line, so that one helps most.

prepared.what: Three example payment schedules and the account count
prepared.conclusion: All three examples failed on 12 Oct and have no retry row at all. The other 211 accounts on EE's list have the same failure date.
findings: Every account on EE's list failed on 12 Oct, the bank holiday.
None of them has a retry scheduled, so this is not a bank decline.
unanswered: Whether a later retry would collect both months at once. Only Kraken CE can say.

draft.target: Asana comment on TARIFF-BACKDATE, reply to Hana Mori
draft.body_en:
Hi Hana, thank you for flagging this.

The 96 customers were moved to Green Fixed with a start date of 1 September, after their September bills had already been issued. When a tariff starts in a period that has already been billed, Kraken reissues that bill at the new rate. That is the second bill they received.

There are two ways to avoid this next time:
1. Start the new tariff from the next billing period, so no issued bill is touched.
2. Keep the backdated start, and send customers a short notice before the corrected bill goes out.

Which would suit EE better? We will send the credit amount for each customer separately once it is confirmed.

issue: 96 customers got a second September bill after EE moved them to a new tariff starting 1 Sep.
This is how a backdated tariff works, so the fix is a choice about how EE enter them.
